notes: Teaching/receptive/production roles must be reviewed pedagogically. Some ledger introduction placements conflict with U1-L01 canonical brief; never expand the lesson solely to turn the report green. Review == agent source review, not human approval.

items.label: Can understand basic phrases in short, simple texts. (P)
items.rationale: This objective includes reading short texts, but the listening-led first-contact chapter has no authored reading check; discuss cross-skill placement.

items.label: Can understand the main information when people introduce themselves (e.g. ‘name’, ‘age’, ‘where they are from’). (P)
items.rationale: Source ability includes name, age and origin examples, while the locked U1-L01 brief limits this chapter to names; keep age/origin for later approved lessons.

items.label: Can follow speech which is very slow and carefully articulated, with long pauses. (Ca)
items.rationale: Ensure first listening audio is learner-paced, and enable focused replay of clearly articulated first-contact lines.

items.label: Can give key information to introduce themselves (e.g. ‘name’, ‘age’, ‘where they are from’). (P)
items.rationale: Source ability includes name, age and origin examples, while the locked U1-L01 brief limits this chapter to names; keep age/origin for later approved lessons.

items.label: Can ask and answer simple questions in areas of immediate need or on very familiar topics. (Ca)
items.rationale: This first-contact interaction can assess one short exchange in which the learner responds and initiates a relevant personal question.

items.label: Can accurately repeat clearly spoken words, phrases, and short sentences. (P)
items.rationale: A1 repetition skill can be supported by optional phrase echoes, but MC screenshots alone cannot verify accurate vocal repetition.

items.label: Can introduce themselves, their hobbies and interests in a basic way. (CJa)
items.rationale: The broader source ability covers hobbies and interests, but this lesson brief explicitly limits production to first-contact name and wellbeing.

items.label: Can make an introduction and use basic greeting and leave-taking expressions. (C)
items.rationale: Simple leave-taking naturally ends the recorded exchange and optional final Speaking; do not turn it into a separate exit-mastery gate.

items.label: Good morning
items.rationale: Teach as the time-of-day greeting before listening and let the learner use it naturally in a changed first meeting.

items.label: How are you?
items.rationale: Introduce the wellbeing question with the recorded exchange and elicit an independent use in final first-meeting Speaking.

items.label: pretty good
items.rationale: Show one natural positive reply inside the wellbeing teaching and accept it productively in changed-context Speaking.

items.label: really good
items.rationale: Contrast this stronger positive reply with pretty good; invite learner production without inventing a grammar-comparison target.

items.label: Thank you
items.rationale: Explain short politeness response from authored audio and require natural polite response in final unscripted first-contact speaking.

items.label: FORM: PREDICATIVE, WITH 'BE'
items.rationale: Teach minimum I am / I'm in familiar first-contact utterances, not the broader grammatical category or a full paradigm.

items.label: FORM: AFFIRMATIVE DECLARATIVE
items.rationale: Provide I am and My name is affirmative examples as supports only, without promoting every declarative form into an independent A1 target.

items.label: FORM: NEGATIVE DECLARATIVE WITH 'BE'
items.rationale: Negative be is present in the ledger but not in the narrow first-contact brief; adding a negative conjugation drill would exceed scope.

items.label: FORM: WITH NOUNS
items.rationale: Use name slot My name is Leo naturally without requiring an independent nouns grammar exercise.

items.label: FORM: MAIN VERB 'BE'
items.rationale: Model first-person be in I am and I'm with a simple name; broader be system deliberately deferred.

items.label: FORM: (SUBJECT) STATEMENTS
items.rationale: Use basic subject plus be statements only as formulaic contexts, not a general syntax lesson.

items.label: FORM: LINKING VERB, 'BE'
items.rationale: I am Maya and I'm fine give familiar linking-be context; this is one integrated chunk, not a separate chart.

items.label: FORM: 'BE' + COMPLEMENT
items.rationale: Use I'm Maya and I'm okay as short meaningful chunks, without generalizing beyond scope.

items.label: advice
items.rationale: Coverage ledger introduces this item in first-contact lesson even though the canonical brief does not teach advice; needs an explicit approved disposition.

items.label: afraid
items.rationale: Afraid is a wider feelings adjective; no separate productive or receptive teaching requirement is established in the narrow introduction brief.

items.label: be
items.rationale: Controlled as a grammar/function system in I am and I'm; avoid declaring separate dictionary-word lexical mastery.

items.label: excited
items.rationale: Level-wide productive adjective does not automatically belong to this first-contact script; review scope and lifecycle without forcing an extra feelings chart.

items.label: feeling
items.rationale: Word has a level-wide productive role but the locked first-contact brief is narrow; curriculum reviewer must decide whether it belongs in this opening lesson.

items.label: its
items.rationale: Possessive its is not taught by the minimum first/second person be chunk in the lesson brief; grammar owner should review placement.

items.label: nothing
items.rationale: The target word does not arise naturally in the approved basic first-contact goal and should not become a random vocabulary card.

items.label: people
items.rationale: Incidental classroom-context noun for two people meeting; should not be a mandatory independent production target.

items.label: photograph
items.rationale: Photograph is tied to this lesson in the ledger but not to greeting, names or wellbeing; requires curriculum review rather than invented picture dialogue.

items.label: sad
items.rationale: Sad is a broader feelings item outside core short positive wellbeing answers; reviewer should decide teaching placement.

items.label: thanks
items.rationale: Teach the everyday politeness word in I'm fine, thanks; it is a spoken formula here, not an unrelated dictionary card.

items.label: tired
items.rationale: Tired is a wider wellbeing adjective than the authored beginner first-meeting exchange; scope must be approved.

items.label: yourself
items.rationale: Reflexive yourself would introduce unsupported complexity beyond the initial greetings and name exchange; must be reviewed.

items.label: Sound perception and word recognition
items.rationale: First uninterrupted listening, then focused replays train recognition of names and greetings at realistic learner-paced speech.

items.label: Intonation, interaction, and stance
items.rationale: Contrast rising-question intonation in What's your name? and How are you? with the natural reply during focused listening and Speaking.
